title: ClientConfigResponse.parsedUpdatedAt rejects timestamps used by the tests
reasoning: parsedUpdatedAt only uses the fractional-seconds ISO8601 formatter. The linked config test uses an updated_at value without fractional seconds, and the same file's general toISO8601Date helper explicitly supports that format. Any consumer using parsedUpdatedAt for conflict detection or freshness checks will get nil for a timestamp shape already treated as valid elsewhere.
reproduction: Decode the testClientConfigResponseDecoding fixture, then call response.parsedUpdatedAt(); it returns nil for 2026-01-26T15:00:00.
recommendation: Implement parsedUpdatedAt as updatedAt.toISO8601Date() so it shares the same accepted timestamp formats as the rest of the client.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing config test decodes updated_at but never asserts parsedUpdatedAt, so the helper can reject the fixture format without failing.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend testClientConfigResponseDecoding to assert response.parsedUpdatedAt() is non-nil for 2026-01-26T15:00:00 and add a fractional-seconds case.
minimumFixScope: One-line change in ClientConfigResponse.parsedUpdatedAt plus a focused model test.
